_comment: Where tools/title_progress.py finds Call of Duty: Black Ops and what cannot be read from its sources. Paths are this machine's checkouts; nothing of the title is in this repository.
name: Call of Duty: Black Ops

sys.where: every call the game imports exists in `any360::sys` (the four only this game uses were added for it), but the game does not run on the full binding yet: it stops after its first network calls (see known problems). Opt-in: `--any360_sys_groups=stateless,files,objects,threads,memory,xam,input,audio`

gfx.where: opt-in: `--any360_gpu=true`; the game draws its first scenes through `any360::gfx` at 60 FPS (1,400 to 1,700 draws a frame), on ReXGlue's kernel
todo: Check what is drawn against ReXGlue's GPU, scene by scene, beyond the first minute.

next: A network layer in `any360::sys`: the game runs a local server over loopback sockets even in solo play, and Any360 answers today as a console with no network (every socket call fails, no XNADDR). Until then the game's network calls stay on ReXGlue's runtime (`--any360_sys_runtime_calls=NetDll_...`), and mixing the two kernels stops it.
Then every system group on `any360::sys` through the campaign and Zombies: saves, sound, the gamepad.
Find the XDK and C runtime functions Any360 already has (`memcpy`, `memset`, the string functions) in this executable and bind them after a check in game.
open: With every system group on `any360::sys` and the network on ReXGlue's runtime, the game stops a few seconds in, reading through a null pointer right after `XNetQosLookup` (answered by the runtime).

With only some groups switched, the game can report a missing asset (`couldn't find shell shock 'flashbang'`) or stop drawing: each group alone needs the others' objects (events, APCs, completion ports), so those runs say little; the full binding is what counts.
